mainTopic: Reversing a mistaken money ruling: several answers to the contradiction between our משנה and the משנה in בכורות
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier teaching: in דיני נפשות, the court begins its discussion with reasons to acquit. Then the גמרא quotes our משנה, which says a money ruling can be reopened. It contrasts this with a משנה in בכורות, which says a judge's mistaken ruling stays in place (מה שעשה עשוי) and the judge pays from his own money. רב יוסף splits the cases by expert versus non-expert, but this answer is rejected. רב נחמן then splits them by whether a greater court exists to review the ruling. רב ששת splits them by the type of mistake: an error in דבר משנה is reversed, while an error in שיקול הדעת stands. The גמרא then defines both terms. רב המנונא challenges רב ששת from the story of רבי טרפון and the cow, and רבא explains the force of that challenge. Finally, רב חסדא splits the cases by whether the judge physically handed over the item. The גמרא rereads our משנה to fit his answer, and the comparison to capital cases continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Capital cases open with reasons to acquit
steps.stepSummary: The earlier teaching ends with its lesson: in דיני נפשות, the court begins its discussion with reasons to acquit.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that in capital cases, the court begins the discussion with reasons to find the accused innocent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier teaching by stating the lesson that comes out of it. In capital cases, the judges begin with reasons to acquit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line wraps up a discussion that started earlier on the דף. It confirms that in דיני נפשות, the court's first words must lean toward זכות (acquittal). The lesson is now fully stated, and the גמרא can move on.

keyTerms.meaning: From here; we learn from this source
They open; the court begins its discussion
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
Toward acquittal; in the accused's favor

steps.whatToRemember: In דיני נפשות, the court always opens its discussion with reasons to acquit.

phrases.english: From here we learn that in capital cases they open
first with a reason to acquit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיכָּן שֶׁפּוֹתְחִין בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת תְּחִלָּה לִזְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the earlier discussion on the דף by stating its final lesson.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In capital cases, deliberation must open with an argument for acquittal.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: money cases can be reopened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה: in דיני ממונות, a ruling can be reopened and reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: in money cases, the court brings the case back to be judged again, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from our משנה to start a new discussion. This line sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה teaches that in money cases, a ruling can be reopened, whether to clear someone or to make him pay. The word כו׳ means the rest of the משנה line is assumed. The גמרא brings it up now because it is about to compare it with a different משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases
They bring the case back; they reopen and reverse the ruling
And so on; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Money cases: they bring back for retrial, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In money cases, a ruling may be reopened and reversed.

steps.title: A contradiction: a judge's mistaken ruling stays in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that says when a judge rules wrongly, the ruling stands and the judge pays from his own money. This seems to say a mistaken ruling cannot be reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with another source: if a judge decided a case, cleared the one who should pay, made the innocent one pay, called something pure impure, or called something impure pure, what he did is done, and he pays from his own pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets another משנה against ours. That משנה seems to say a judge's mistaken ruling cannot be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says money rulings can be reversed. The other משנה says a mistaken ruling stays in place (מה שעשה עשוי) and the judge must pay for the loss he caused. If the ruling could just be reversed, there would be nothing for the judge to pay. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: They contrasted it; the גמרא raises a contradicting source
What he did is done; the ruling stays in place
He pays from his own pocket
He ruled something impure / he ruled something pure

phrases.english: And they contrasted it with another source:
phrases.notes: The source is a משנה in בכורות 28b.

phrases.english: If a judge decided a case,

phrases.aramaic: זִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב, חִיֵּיב אֶת הַזַּכַּאי,
phrases.english: cleared the one who should pay, made the innocent one pay,

phrases.aramaic: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר, טִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא –
phrases.english: called a pure item impure, called an impure item pure –
what he did is done,
and he must pay from his own house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 2 with a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule that money rulings can be reopened
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in בכורות says a mistaken ruling stays in place and the judge pays, which means it cannot be reversed. That contradicts our משנה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: expert judge versus non-expert judge
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that our משנה is about an expert judge, whose ruling can be reversed. The משנה in בכורות is about a non-expert judge, whose ruling stays in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a problem. Here it is talking about an expert judge, and there it is talking about a judge who is not an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף settles the contradiction by saying each משנה is talking about a different kind of judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, when an expert judge (מומחה) errs, the case is reopened. When a non-expert errs, his ruling stays and he pays for the loss. The two sources no longer clash, because they describe different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem; the start of an answer
Here... there; each source is about a different case
An expert judge

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult,
here it is about an expert,
phrases.notes: "Here" is our משנה, where the ruling gets reversed.

phrases.english: there it is about one who is not an expert.
phrases.notes: "There" is the משנה in בכורות, where the ruling stays and he pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different kind of judge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be talking about the same kind of judge.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about an expert judge, and בכורות is about a non-expert judge.

steps.title: Challenge: an expert's ruling also stays in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף from the very same משנה in בכורות. It says an expert who erred is exempt from paying, which shows his ruling stays in place too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a case with an expert really reopened? But the משנה teaches: if he was an expert approved by the court, he is exempt from paying!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's answer, using a later line from the same משנה in בכורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in בכורות also discusses an expert judge and says he is exempt from paying. That exemption only matters if his mistaken ruling actually stands and someone lost money. So even an expert's ruling is not reversed, and רב יוסף's split does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught; this introduces a source that challenges what was just said
An expert approved by the court
Exempt from paying

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not that the expert is exempt. The proof is that he needs an exemption at all. If his ruling were simply reversed, nobody would have lost money, so there would be nothing to be exempt from.

phrases.english: And with an expert do they bring it back for retrial?
But it is taught:
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same משנה in בכורות.

phrases.english: If he was an expert approved by the court –
he is exempt from paying!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that an expert's ruling is reversed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An expert would not need an exemption from paying unless his mistaken ruling stood. So an expert's ruling is not reversed either.

steps.title: רב נחמן: it depends on whether a greater court exists
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that a ruling is reversed when there is a court greater in wisdom and number. When no greater court exists, the ruling stays in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Here it is talking about a case where there is a court greater than this one in wisdom and in number. There it is talking about a case where there is no court greater than this one in wisdom and in number.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new way to settle the contradiction. Instead of looking at the judge's own skill, he looks at whether a higher court exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה, which reverses the ruling, is about a case where a greater court can review the decision. The משנה in בכורות, where the ruling stays, is about a case with no greater court to fix the mistake. So the deciding factor is whether a higher authority exists that can review the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Greater than him; a court that ranks higher
In wisdom
In number; how many scholars or students it has

steps.whatToRemember: A mistaken money ruling is reversed only if a greater court (גדול הימנו בחכמה ובמנין) exists to review it. Otherwise, מה שעשה עשוי: the ruling stays in place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shifts the question from the judge's own qualifications to whether there is a higher court that can review his decision.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
here, where there is one greater than him
phrases.notes: "Here" is our משנה, where the ruling gets reversed.

phrases.english: in wisdom and in number,
phrases.notes: "Number" means how many scholars or students that court has.

phrases.english: there, where there is no one greater than him
in wisdom and in number.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כָּאן שֶׁיֵּשׁ גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the contradiction in step 3, after רב יוסף's answer was rejected in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by whether a higher court exists
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף thought the difference was the judge's own expertise.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ruling is reversed only where a greater court exists to review it. Otherwise, the ruling stays in place.

steps.title: רב ששת: It depends on the kind of mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by splitting between two kinds of error: an error in a clear source (דבר משנה), where the ruling is reversed, and an error in judgment (שיקול הדעת), where it stands. He backs this with his own teaching in the name of רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Our משנה, which says the ruling is reversed, is where the judge made a mistake about a clear משנה. The other משנה, which says the ruling stands, is where he made a mistake in weighing the opinions. As רב ששת said in the name of רב אסי: If he erred in a clear משנה, the ruling is reversed. If he erred in weighing the opinions, it is not reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a new answer to the contradiction between the two משניות. He says the difference is not who the judge is but what kind of mistake he made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף split by the judge (expert or not), and רב נחמן split by whether a greater court exists. רב ששת splits by the type of error instead. If the judge missed a clear source, his ruling has no standing and is reversed. If he chose one side of an open debate, his ruling stays.

keyTerms.meaning: He erred in a clear, known source, like ruling against an explicit משנה
Weighing of opinions; a judgment call between views
Goes back; the ruling is reversed
Does not go back; the ruling stays in place

steps.whyThisMatters: This split between דבר משנה and שיקול הדעת becomes a basic rule for judging mistaken rulings.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Here, it is where he erred in a matter of Mishnah;
phrases.notes: The first 'here' is our משנה, which says the ruling is reversed.

phrases.english: there, it is where he erred in weighing the opinions.
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the משנה in בכורות, which says the ruling stands.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: As Rav Sheshet said in the name of Rav Asi:
If he erred in a matter of Mishnah, the ruling is reversed;
if he erred in weighing the opinions, it is not reversed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: כָּאן שֶׁטָּעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third resolution of the contradiction from step 3, after רב יוסף and רב נחמן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each משנה is about a different type of error.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to give opposite rules for every mistaken ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about an error in a clear source, which is reversed. The משנה in בכורות is about an error in weighing opinions, which stands.

steps.title: How far does 'a clear source' reach?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether an error against later authorities also counts as an error in דבר משנה. He goes step by step: רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, then רב and שמואל, then רבינא and רב אשי themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Does it count even if he erred about a teaching of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא? He said: Yes. Even about a teaching of רב and שמואל? He said: Yes. Even about teachings of mine and yours?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tests how wide the category of דבר משנה is. Each question moves to a later generation of rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Does 'משנה' mean only the actual משנה, or any accepted teaching? רב אשי agrees it includes the last תנאים and the early אמוראים. The last question, about רבינא and רב אשי themselves, gets its answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Mine and yours

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ טָעָה בְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא?
phrases.english: Even if he erred about a teaching of Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Oshaya?
He said to him: Yes.
Even about a teaching of Rav and Shmuel?
He said to him: Yes.
Even about teachings of mine and yours?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ טָעָה בְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the scope of the term דבר משנה introduced by רב ששת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an error against later authorities, even the current generation, count as an error in דבר משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes for רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, and yes for רב and שמואל. The last question is answered in the next step.

steps.title: רב אשי: Our teachings count too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that even the teachings of רבינא and himself count as a clear source. They are not 'reed-cutters in the marsh'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are we just reed-cutters in the marsh?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the last question with a sharp rhetorical line. Their own teachings also count, so an error against them is also reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reed-cutter is a simple laborer whose words carry no weight. By saying 'we are not reed-cutters', רב אשי means that accepted rulings of his generation are as binding as earlier ones. Going against them counts as an error in דבר משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it so that...? (opens a rhetorical question)
Cutters of reeds in the marsh; simple people with no authority

phrases.english: He said to him: Are we, then,
cutters of reeds in the marsh?
phrases.notes: He means: we are not nobodies. Our accepted teachings count as a clear source too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's final question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Even the teachings of רבינא and רב אשי count as a clear source, so ruling against them is an error in דבר משנה.

steps.title: What counts as an error in weighing opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of שיקול הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of an error in weighing the opinions?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what an error in a clear source is, the גמרא asks what the other kind of error looks like. This question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even recent teachings count as a clear source, it is unclear what is left for שיקול הדעת. The גמרא wants a concrete case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case of an error in weighing the opinions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the reach of דבר משנה, turns to define the other category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of an error in שיקול הדעת.

steps.title: רב פפא defines an error in judgment
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the case. Two תנאים or two אמוראים disagree, and no ruling was given for either side. The judge follows one view, while common practice follows the other. That is an error in שיקול הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For example, two תנאים or two אמוראים disagree with each other, and no ruling was stated like either one. The judge happened to act like one of them, but the common practice follows the other. That is an error in weighing the opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the definition. The judge did not go against any clear ruling. He picked the side that most others do not follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case there is no clear source he went against, since the הלכה was never decided. His mistake is only that he went against the general practice. So his ruling is a judgment call, and it is not reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sages of the משנה era / sages of the גמרא era
They disagree with each other
Not like this master and not like that master
The common flow of the הלכה; how judges usually rule

steps.whatToRemember: An error in a clear source, even a teaching of recent אמוראים, is reversed. Picking the less accepted side of an undecided debate is שיקול הדעת, and the ruling stands.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי אוֹ תְּרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי
phrases.english: For example, two Tannaim or two Amoraim
who disagree with each other,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אִיתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּמָר וְלָא כְּמָר,
phrases.english: and the halacha was not stated like this one or like that one,
and it happened that he acted like one of them,
and the common practice goes like the other one –
that is an error in weighing the opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שיקול הדעת is when the judge followed one side of an undecided debate while common practice follows the other side.

steps.title: רב המנונא begins a challenge from the cow of בית מנחם
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא challenges רב ששת. He quotes the story in the משנה in בכורות about a cow whose womb was removed. רבי טרפון fed it to the dogs, meaning he treated it as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא challenged רב ששת: There was a story with a cow of the household of מנחם whose womb was removed, and רבי טרפון fed it to the dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא starts an objection to רב ששת by bringing a story from the same משנה in בכורות. Here the גמרא is only setting up the story. The point of the challenge comes in the lines that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון ruled that the cow was forbidden, so it was given to dogs. The story is brought to test רב ששת's rule about which mistakes are reversed. How exactly it challenges him becomes clear as the story continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Her womb was removed

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection to Rav Sheshet:
There was an incident with a cow of the household of Menachem
whose womb was removed,
phrases.notes: Here 'הָאֵם' means the womb, not the mother.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Tarfon fed it to the dogs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the terms are defined, turns to attack רב ששת's main distinction from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that an error in דבר משנה is reversed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case of רבי טרפון's ruling on the cow will be used to test whether a mistaken ruling was really reversed. The argument is finished in the continuation of the story.

steps.title: The rest of the cow story: the חכמים permit it and רבי עקיבא exempts רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues. The חכמים in יבנה permitted a cow whose womb was removed, based on what תודוס the doctor reported. רבי טרפון feared he would have to pay, but רבי עקיבא told him an accepted expert is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before the חכמים in יבנה, and they permitted the cow. תודוס the doctor said that cows and pigs leave Alexandria only after their wombs are cut out, so they cannot give birth. רבי טרפון said: 'Your donkey is gone, Tarfon!' רבי עקיבא told him: 'You are exempt, because any accepted expert of the public is exempt from paying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the משנה that רב המנונא brought. This step gives the end of the story, which is the material his challenge will use in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals from Alexandria live normally without a womb, so removing it does not make an animal a טריפה. That means רבי טרפון ruled wrongly when he treated the cow as forbidden. רבי עקיבא exempts him from paying only because he was a recognized expert.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual case or incident
יבנה, where the חכמים had their court
תודוס the doctor
Cutting out the womb
A judge accepted as an expert by the public
Exempt from paying

phrases.english: And the case came before the Sages in Yavne,
and they permitted it.
For Todos the doctor said:
No cow or pig goes out
from Alexandria of Egypt

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חוֹתְכִין הָאֵם שֶׁלָּהּ,
phrases.english: unless they cut out its womb,
so that it will not give birth.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: הָלְכָה חֲמוֹרְךָ, טַרְפוֹן!
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said: Your donkey is gone, Tarfon!
phrases.notes: He means he has lost his own property, because he thinks he must pay the owner back for the cow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: פָּטוּר אַתָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: You are exempt,
for anyone who is an accepted expert for the public
is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quote that רב המנונא started in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's distinction between an error in דבר משנה and an error in שיקול הדעת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step supplies the source material: רבי עקיבא exempts רבי טרפון only because he is an expert, and says nothing about the ruling being reversed.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי עקיבא just say the ruling is reversed?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא makes his attack. If רב ששת is right, רבי עקיבא should have said that רבי טרפון erred in a clear source, so his ruling is simply reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רב ששת's view is correct, רבי עקיבא should have told him: 'You erred in דבר משנה, and when someone errs in דבר משנה, the ruling is reversed.'
steps.whatsHappening: Here רב המנונא spells out his challenge. He points to what רבי עקיבא did not say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law about a cow without a womb is a clear, written ruling, so רבי טרפון's mistake was an error in דבר משנה. Under רב ששת, that kind of error is simply reversed and nobody pays. So why did רבי עקיבא give the 'expert' reason instead?

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (if your view is right)
Let him say to him
One who errs against a clear, known ruling
Goes back; the ruling is reversed

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רב ששת's rule about the two kinds of mistakes is correct.

phrases.english: let him say to him:
phrases.notes: Let רבי עקיבא say this to רבי טרפון.

phrases.english: You erred in a matter of Mishnah,
and when one errs in a matter of Mishnah, the ruling goes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the story quoted in steps 12-13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's rule that an error in דבר משנה is reversed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא used the 'expert' exemption, which fits an error in שיקול הדעת, even though this was an error in דבר משנה. That suggests רב ששת's distinction is wrong.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gave one reason and then added a second
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא was saying two things. First, this was an error in דבר משנה, so the ruling is reversed. Second, even if it had been an error in judgment, an accepted expert is exempt from paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was saying 'one reason, and another.' One reason: you erred in דבר משנה, and such a ruling is reversed. Another reason: even if you erred in שיקול הדעת, you are an accepted expert, and every accepted expert is exempt from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It says רבי עקיבא really meant both reasons, but the משנה only spelled out the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's words do not contradict רב ששת. His first, hidden reason is exactly רב ששת's rule. The expert reason is an extra 'and besides' argument for the case where the mistake was only in judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: One reason, and another besides
Alternatively; even if
Judgment in weighing between opinions (defined in step 11)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's statement has two layers: (1) an error in דבר משנה is simply reversed, and (2) even an error in שיקול הדעת is exempt for an accepted expert. Steps 16-17 come back to רב המנונא's challenge and sharpen it.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:
One: that you erred in a matter of Mishnah,
and when one errs in a matter of Mishnah, the ruling goes back.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: אִי נָמֵי בְּשִׁיקּוּל הַדַּעַת טָעִיתָ –
phrases.english: And another: even if you erred in judgment,
you are an accepted expert for the public,
and anyone who is an accepted expert for the public is exempt from paying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב המנונא's challenge from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the statement holds two reasons, and only the second is spelled out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's only reason was the expert exemption, which would contradict רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא first meant that the ruling is reversed, and then added the expert exemption as a backup reason.

steps.title: How could the cow story challenge רב ששת at all?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא why רב המנונא even brought this story. The cow had already been fed to the dogs, so there was nothing left to reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: What is רב המנונא challenging רב ששת with, from the cow? The cow was already fed to the dogs, and it is not there for the ruling to be reversed!
steps.whatsHappening: A later אמורא questions whether רב המנונא's challenge made sense to begin with. This sets up a discussion of what רב ששת meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The ruling is reversed' only helps when the item still exists. Here the cow had been destroyed, so רבי עקיבא could not have said 'it goes back.' It seems he had no choice but to use the expert exemption, so the story should not challenge רב ששת at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he challenging with?
He fed it to the dogs
It isn't there to be returned or reversed

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
What is Rav Hamnuna objecting with
against Rav Sheshet, from the cow?
The cow, after all, he fed to the dogs,
and it is no longer there to go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מוֹתֵיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back and questions the basis of רב המנונא's challenge from steps 12-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's use of the cow story as a challenge to רב ששת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reversal is impossible once the item is destroyed. So the story's silence about reversal proves nothing against רב ששת.

steps.title: רבא explains what רב המנונא was really proving
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב המנונא's proof was never about reversing the cow ruling. It was about why רבי טרפון was afraid he would have to pay at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רב המנונא meant to tell רב ששת. Suppose you hold that an error in a clear source is not reversed, so the ruling stands. Then it makes sense that רבי טרפון was afraid, and that רבי עקיבא told him an accepted expert is exempt from paying. But suppose you hold that such an error is reversed. Then רבי עקיבא should have told him: if the cow were still here, your ruling would count for nothing, so you did nothing. Now too you did nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's question from step 16. The proof is not about reversing anything. It is about רבי טרפון's fear of paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mistake in a clear source makes a ruling void, then רבי טרפון's ruling 'did nothing,' and the loss came from the owner feeding the cow to the dogs. In that case רבי טרפון had no reason to fear paying. His fear only makes sense if the ruling stands, which works against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant
Evidently, it turns out that
The ruling stands
You did nothing (your act had no legal effect)

phrases.english: This is what he was saying to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is explaining what רב המנונא was telling רב ששת.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
one who errs in a clear source does not reverse,
then evidently the ruling stands —
that is why Rabbi Tarfon was afraid,
and he said to him:
You are an expert accepted by the court
and you are exempt from paying.
But if you say
one who errs in a clear source reverses,
let him say to him:
Since if the cow were still here,
your ruling would not be a ruling
and you would have done nothing,
now too you did nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's question about the point of רב המנונא's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the proof: it comes from רבי טרפון's fear of paying, not from reversing the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The proof seemed pointless, because the cow was gone and nothing could be reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי טרפון's fear shows the ruling stood, which works against רב ששת's view that it is void.

steps.title: רב חסדא: did the judge physically carry out the ruling?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא settles the contradiction between the two משניות. In בכורות the judge himself took the item and handed it over, so he pays. In our משנה he did not, so the ruling is reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Here (in בכורות) it is a case where the judge took the item and handed it over with his own hand. Here (in our משנה) it is a case where he did not take it and hand it over himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new answer to the contradiction between our משנה, where the ruling is reversed, and the משנה in בכורות, where the judge pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא does not split the cases by the type of error. He splits them by what the judge did. If the judge physically carried out his own ruling, he caused the loss himself, so he pays. If he only gave a ruling, the court simply reverses it.

keyTerms.meaning: Took and gave with the hand: the judge personally moved the item from one side to the other
Here: pointing to one of the two sources being contrasted

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new way to settle the contradiction that does not depend on the kind of mistake the judge made.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Here, where he took and gave with his hand,
phrases.notes: This first "here" is the משנה in בכורות, where the judge must pay.

phrases.english: here, where he did not take and give with his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: כָּאן שֶׁנָּטַל וְנָתַן בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the רב ששת and רב המנונא discussion to give a new answer to the contradiction between the two משניות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by whether the judge physically carried out the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to disagree about whether a mistaken ruling is reversed or the judge pays.
steps.terutzMaskana: The judge pays only when he personally took the item and handed it over. Otherwise the ruling is reversed.

steps.title: How can 'exempting the liable' involve handing anything over?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב חסדא's answer fits the case in בכורות where the judge exempted someone who was really liable. In that case nothing gets physically handed over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, 'he made the innocent liable' works, such as where the judge took the item and handed it over. But 'he exempted the liable,' how can you find that? The judge just told him 'You are exempt,' and he did not take and hand over anything with his hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The משנה in בכורות also makes the judge pay for wrongly exempting someone, and there no item was physically moved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making someone liable can involve the judge taking money and handing it over. Exempting someone involves only words. So the case of exempting seems to fall outside רב חסדא's rule, yet בכורות still says the judge pays.

keyTerms.meaning: He made the innocent party liable
He exempted the party who was really liable
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: Granted, "he made the innocent liable" works,
phrases.notes: These are cases from the משנה in בכורות where the judge has to pay.

phrases.english: such as where he took and gave with his hand.
But "he exempted the liable,"
how can you find it?
He just told him, "You are exempt,"
but he did not take and give with his hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב חסדא's answer against the case of wrongly exempting someone.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the judge pays only when he physically handed something over.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exempting someone involves only words, yet the משנה in בכורות makes the judge pay for it.

steps.title: Saying 'you are exempt' counts as handing it over
steps.stepSummary: Telling someone 'you are exempt' counts as if the judge took the item and handed it over himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said 'You are exempt,' it is as if he took the item and handed it over with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words 'You are exempt' are the same as physically carrying out the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a judge exempts someone, nothing more needs to be done. The money simply stays where it is. So the judge's words already finish the job, which is just like handing it over himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is considered as if he took and gave with his hand

phrases.english: Since he said, "You are exempt,"
it is as if he took and gave with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the case of exempting someone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening what counts as 'taking and giving with the hand.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only physically moving an item counts as carrying out the ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying 'You are exempt' already finishes the ruling, so it counts as handing it over.

steps.title: Then how can our משנה ever reverse a ruling to make someone liable?
steps.stepSummary: The answer in step 20 causes a new problem. Our משנה says money rulings are reversed in both directions. But if 'You are exempt' always counts as handing it over, a ruling could never be reversed to make someone liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about our משנה, which teaches that in money cases a ruling is reversed whether to acquit or to convict? Granted, reversing to acquit works: the judge first said 'You are liable' and did not take and hand over anything. But reversing to convict, how can you find it? Where the judge said 'You are exempt'? But you just said that once he says 'You are exempt,' it is as if he took and handed it over!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against רב חסדא. A reversal that makes someone liable now seems impossible, yet our משנה says it happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reversing to make someone liable can only happen after the judge said 'You are exempt.' But step 20 said those words count as handing it over, and then the judge should pay instead of reversing. So the case our משנה describes seems to have no room in רב חסדא's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Money cases
We reverse (bring the case back to be judged again)
To acquit
To convict, to make liable
At first, originally

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this challenge comes from outside. It is caused by the answer the גמרא itself just gave in step 20.

phrases.english: But our Mishnah, which teaches:
In money cases we reverse
whether to acquit or to convict,
granted, reversing to acquit, you can find it,
where at first he told him, "You are liable,"
and he did not take and did not give with his hand.
But reversing to convict, how can you find it?
Where he told him, "You are exempt"?
But you said:
since he told him, "You are exempt,"
it is as if he took and gave with his hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 20 to raise a new difficulty from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's approach, together with the rule that 'You are exempt' counts as handing it over.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If saying 'You are exempt' counts as handing it over, a ruling could never be reversed to make someone liable. That goes against our משנה, which says rulings are reversed in both directions.

steps.title: The משנה is really teaching one reversal, not two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה teaches only one case. In דיני ממונות, a ruling is reversed to exempt the defendant, and that same reversal is a loss for the other litigant. It then starts the matching rule for דיני נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches only one thing. In money cases the court reverses a ruling to exempt someone, and that exemption is a loss for the other side. The matching rule in capital cases is that the court reverses a ruling to acquit...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21. It says the משנה never meant two different reversals in money cases. It only meant one reversal, which helps one side and hurts the other. The last words begin a comparison to capital cases that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 asked how a money ruling could ever be reversed toward liability, since saying 'you are exempt' already counts as handing the item over. The answer is that the משנה only means reversing toward exemption. In a money case, though, one person's exemption is the other person's loss, so the משנה can still describe it as reversing 'to liability' from the other side's point of view.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches only one thing (one case, not two)
They bring back, meaning they reverse or re-judge the ruling
In favor, toward exemption or acquittal
Liability, a loss for someone
The matching case, the parallel to it
Capital cases, where a life is at stake

steps.confusionAlert: In a money case there are always two sides. 'To exempt' and 'to liability' are not two different reversals here. They are the same single reversal, seen from the defendant's side and from the claimant's side.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב חסדא's approach. Money rulings are only reversed toward exemption, and that fits the idea that 'you are exempt' counts as handing over the item.

phrases.english: It teaches only one thing:
In money cases, they reverse the ruling to exempt,
which is liability.
phrases.notes: He means it is a loss for the other litigant. When the defendant is exempted, the claimant loses.

phrases.english: The matching case with regard to capital cases:
they reverse the ruling to acquit,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. The גמרא finishes it on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 21 by rereading the משנה's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: two phrases describe one event from two sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say money rulings are reversed in two directions: to exempt and to make liable
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only reversal toward exemption. That same reversal is 'liability' for the other litigant, so רב חסדא's approach still stands.
